title: Lobosky, Max Finkman's group and its clarinetists
summary: Allen asks about pianist Lobosky, who was a semi-jazz player with Max Finkman; they recall Red Bowman, Tony Parenti and a forgotten clarinetist's style.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Who were the great clarinetists? Favorites and rivals

blocks.x: What kind of piano player was Lobosky?

Oh, Lobosky was a fine, talented piano player. He wasn't much a jazz man, though, but I mean he was what you call a semi-jazz man. He could read and play any kind of a show that came along, but he could play some jazz too. But I mean he couldn't play like the man that featured more today, because he was a different class musician than us. In other words, he was first class musician, I'd say. Who was he playing with?
